title: [14/1/2023] The percentage of workers from five different European countries
prompt: The graph below shows the percentage of workers from five different European countries that were absent for a day or more due to illness from 1991 to 2001. Summarise the information by selecting reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the percentage of workers who took sick leave in five European countries over a period of 10 years, from 1991 to 2001.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while the Netherlands and Sweden showed an upward trend in illness absence rates, France experienced a significant decline. Meanwhile, the figures for the UK and Germany remained relatively stable throughout the period. In addition, the Netherlands consistently recorded the highest proportion of absent workers among all countries shown.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the countries with noticeable changes, in 1991, both the Netherlands and France started at approximately 5% of workers taking sick leave, while Sweden's figure stood at around 3%. The Dutch rate then fluctuated before dropping to 4% in 1996, after which it rose steadily to reach about 5.5% by 2001. In contrast, the French percentage declined to roughly 3% then leveled off until the end of the period. Sweden, meanwhile, saw a gradual increase from 3% to 4.5% during the same timeframe.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining countries, the UK began the period at 2.5% while Germany was at 1.7%, and despite some minor fluctuations, UK's figure ended at virtually the same level in 2001. Similarly, Germany maintained the lowest absence rate among all five nations, hovering between 1.5% and 2% throughout the entire period.
